issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to mark the end of the main loop with the label `loop_end` (problem_statement.md line 21), but the solution repository uses the label `end_loop` (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm line 17). This naming mismatch between the specification and the reference solution can confuse students about the exact label to add and may break any automated checks or manual verification that expect the exact label `loop_end`.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the label name consistent. Either (A) rename the solution label `end_loop` to `loop_end` so the reference solution matches the problem statement, or (B) update the problem statement to request `end_loop` if that was the intended name. Ensure any automated checks are aligned with the chosen label name.

issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to mark the end of the main loop with the label `loop_end` (problem_statement.md line 21), but the reference solution uses the label `end_loop` (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm line 17). This naming mismatch between the stated requirement and the solution creates a mapping confusion: students comparing their work or relying on the solution for guidance may not recognize `end_loop` as the same required label `loop_end`, and automated checks expecting `loop_end` could report a failure even when the student placed an end-of-loop label.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a single consistent label name across artifacts. For example, rename the label in the solution from `end_loop:` to `loop_end:` (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm line 17) so it matches the problem statement's instruction. Alternatively, update the problem statement to require `end_loop` if that name is preferred.
